bib.title: A Diversity-Promoting Objective Function for Neural Conversation Models

question: Why do SEQ2SEQ conversation models produce generic responses, and can a mutual-information objective at decode time make responses more diverse and relevant?
hypothesis: Maximising likelihood of response given message favours safe high-frequency responses; also weighing the likelihood of the message given the response (MMI) will favour specific responses.
contributions: Propose MMI as objective for neural response generation, in two variants (MMI-antiLM, MMI-bidi) applied only at test time
Show gains in BLEU, distinct-n diversity and human judgments on Twitter and OpenSubtitles

method.summary: Standard maximum-likelihood 4-layer LSTM SEQ2SEQ models p(T|S) and a reversed p(S|T) are trained; the MMI criterion is used only at decoding, either as an anti-language-model penalty on the first gamma tokens (MMI-antiLM) or by reranking a large N-best list with p(S|T) (MMI-bidi). Weights are tuned with MERT on BLEU.

datasets.name: Twitter Conversation Triple Dataset
datasets.split: dev 2118 conversations, test 2114 examples (multi-reference via IR, per Sordoni et al. 2015)
datasets.preprocessing: context limited to the immediately preceding turn; context and message concatenated as source

datasets.name: OpenSubtitles (OSDb)
datasets.size: roughly 60M-70M scripted lines; 20 million conversation pairs used for the Table 1 model
datasets.preprocessing: each subtitle line treated as a full speaker turn

datasets.name: IMSDB
datasets.size: around 0.4 million sentences; dev and test 2k pairs each
datasets.split: random dev and test subsets of 2k pairs each
datasets.preprocessing: consecutive message-response pairs by different characters; source and target length restricted to [6,18]; single reference only

models.name: SEQ2SEQ (4-layer LSTM)
models.architecture: LSTM encoder-decoder, separate parameters per layer

models.name: MMI-antiLM
models.architecture: same SEQ2SEQ, decoding score log p(T|S) - lambda log U(T), plus length bonus

models.name: MMI-bidi
models.architecture: SEQ2SEQ N-best reranked with reverse model p(S|T)

models.name: SMT (Ritter 2011) and SMT+neural reranking (Sordoni 2015)
models.architecture: phrase-based MT (Moses features), optionally reranked with RNN scores and CMM features

other.training_size: roughly 50 million examples; numbers reprinted from Sordoni et al. (2015)

training.objective: maximum likelihood log p(T|S); reverse model p(S|T) trained identically with messages and responses interchanged. MMI used only at test time.
training.regularisation: gradient clipping, scale when norm exceeds 1

other.init: LSTM parameters and embeddings uniform in [-0.08, 0.08]

inference.decoding: beam search, beam size B=200; EOS hypotheses added to N-best list, top B unfinished kept; max length 20
inference.samples: one output per input; N-best list per input much larger than beam size (173 elements on average at beam 20)

parameters.lambda: tuned with MERT (MMI-antiLM on N-best lists; MMI-bidi on dev set); value not stated
parameters.gamma: length-reward weight, tuned with MERT; value not stated
parameters.antiLM_threshold: g(k)=1 if k<=gamma else 0, penalises first gamma tokens; gamma value not stated
parameters.score_antiLM: Score(T) = p(T|S) - lambda U(T) + gamma Nt
parameters.score_bidi: linear combination of p(T|S), lambda p(S|T), gamma Nt

metrics.name: BLEU
metrics.definition: multi-reference on Twitter, single-reference on OpenSubtitles/IMSDB

metrics.name: distinct-1 / distinct-2
metrics.definition: number of distinct unigrams/bigrams divided by total number of generated words

metrics.name: pairwise human preference
metrics.definition: 5 crowd judges per pair on 1000 Twitter test items, prefer more specific outputs, ties allowed; mean of differences

eval.protocol: Human pairwise significance at alpha=0.05 with 95% CIs; no seeds or repeated runs reported; perplexity deliberately not used.

results.claim: MMI-bidi beats the SEQ2SEQ baseline on Twitter BLEU and diversity.
results.setup: Twitter test set, 4-layer SEQ2SEQ trained on 23M instances, beam 200, multi-reference BLEU
results.note: Text later gives MMI-bidi BLEU 5.90 at beam 200 (5.86, 5.76 at 50, 20), which differs from Table 2's 5.22.

results.claim: MMI-bidi reaches 4.44-beating BLEU, above the prior SMT+neural reranking state of the art, with half the training data.
results.setup: SMT+neural reranking trained on roughly 50M examples; MMI-bidi on 23M
results.quote: MT+neural reranking achieves a BLEU score of 4.44

results.claim: MMI-bidi lifts distinct-2 on Twitter from 0.107 to 0.270.
results.table: Table 2, row MMI-bidi, column distinct-2; baseline row SEQ2SEQ (baseline)
results.note: SMT systems still have higher distinct-2 (.351, .358).

results.claim: On OpenSubtitles/IMSDB, MMI-antiLM raises BLEU by 35.9% and distinct-1 by 228% over SEQ2SEQ.
results.setup: trained on OSDb, evaluated on 2k IMSDB pairs, single-reference BLEU
results.table: Table 3, row MMI-antiLM, column BLEU (+35.9%, distinct-1 0.0184 vs 0.0056)
results.note: Table 3 prints distinct-2 gain as 407% without a plus sign.

results.claim: Human judges prefer MMI-bidi to baseline SEQ2SEQ by a mean gain of 0.11.
results.setup: 1000 Twitter test items, 5 judges per pair, 95% CI [0.07, 0.14]
results.note: Gains over SMT 0.29 and SMT+neural reranking 0.28.

results.claim: Mean absolute human rating of MMI-bidi output.
results.setup: 7 judges per output on the 1000-item Twitter sample
results.quote: The mean rating was 3.84 (median: 3.85, 1st Qu: 3.57, 3rd Qu: 4.14)

results.claim: MMI-bidi BLEU degrades only slightly with smaller beams.
results.quote: For MMI-bidi, BLEU scores for beam sizes of 200, 50, 20 are respectively 5.90, 5.86, 5.76.

results.claim: Four generic strings make up 32% of all generated responses of the baseline on OpenSubtitles.
results.setup: SEQ2SEQ baseline outputs; strings I don't know, I don't know what you are talking about, I don't think that is a good idea, Oh my god
results.quote: constitute 32% percent of all generated responses

results.claim: 0.45% of OpenSubtitles training sentences contain I don't know.
results.quote: 0.45% sentences contain the sequence I don’t know

limits: MMI-bidi depends on the N-best list being diverse and needs long N-best lists; reranking is not globally optimal (Sec 4.3.2, 5.3).
MMI-antiLM can give ungrammatical output, fixed with a hard threshold on the first gamma tokens.
MMI is applied only at test time; no jointly trained MMI model.
OpenSubtitles evaluation uses single-reference BLEU so absolute scores are low; text BLEU 5.90 for MMI-bidi conflicts with Table 2 value 5.22.
Values of lambda, gamma and the cutoff are not reported; no seeds or repeat runs; no code or data release stated.
Authors say grounding, persona and intent are left for future work.
